submitted.rationale: Highest measured photocurrent of the three measurements (5.92e-6 A) at Cu 0.40, Fe 0.20, V 0.40. That is close to the Cu2V2O7 stoichiometry with Fe added, a composition region where copper vanadates absorb below 2.72 eV.

rejected.reason: FeVO4-like Fe-rich composition gave only 1.34e-6 A
Cu3V2O8-like Cu-rich composition gave 2.25e-6 A, lower than the balanced Cu:V point

consultations.verdict: Uninformative-to-weakly-supportive: MEGNet HSE gaps of binary end members V2O5 (2.83 eV) and Fe2O3 (2.77 eV) are near/above the 2.72 eV photon energy, so mixed Cu-containing vanadates (lower gap, Cu 3d states) are the more likely absorbers. Index 150 (Cu~V~0.40, Fe 0.20) sits at Cu2V2O7-like stoichiometry with Fe alloying, a known photoanode family; measure as first exploratory point.

Uninformative directly: V2O5 PBE gap 1.18 eV (underestimate; HSE 2.83) confirms vanadate gaps near the 2.72 eV photon energy. Index 110 (Fe 0.47, V 0.42, Cu 0.11) sits near FeVO4 stoichiometry (~2.0-2.1 eV gap, known photoanode), a distinct region from the first measurement, so it explores the Fe-V side.

Weakly against Fe-rich compositions: Fe2O3 gap (PBE 1.53, HSE 2.77) and poor measured Fe-V result (1.3 uA vs 5.9 uA at Cu 0.40) suggest Cu drives performance. Index 141 (Cu 0.53, V 0.35, Fe 0.12) is at Cu3V2O8-like Cu:V ratio with low Fe, extending the trend toward higher Cu.
